moving.title: Moving
oneLiner: A quote-matching service that connects moving customers and movers,
then links them through real-time 1:1 chat once a quote is confirmed

stats.label: Role
stats.sub: FE lead · covered both FE and BE

intro.body: A customer requests quotes with their moving conditions, and movers whose service area and type match send quotes back. The customer compares and confirms one; after that come the deposit payment and 1:1 chat, and once the move is done, the balance payment and a review.

scope.title: Screens
items: Designed shared components (Header, Toast, Skeleton, etc.)
Landing, mover detail and my page
Pending, received and confirmed quote details
Header notification dropdown and 1:1 chat screen

scope.title: API
items: Notification API (REST + real-time delivery over SSE)
Confirmed-quote chat API (Socket.IO, read receipts)
Moved chat message storage to the main DB and S3

scope.title: Structure · Quality
items: Next.js App Router · TypeScript strict setup
Domain-based folder structure and refactoring
Lighthouse-based performance and accessibility improvements
Sitemap · robots.txt · GA consent banner

problems.title: Ghost notifications that said a failed quote had arrived
problems.problem: The quote registration API failed with 409/500, yet the other party's screen showed a "Your quote has arrived" notification, and tapping it led to a 404.
problems.cause: SSE writes to the socket immediately, regardless of whether the transaction commits. Because the notification was created and sent inside the transaction, a later rollback left it on screen but not in the DB.
problems.fix: I split the notification API into create and publishCreated so that saving happens inside the same transaction and sending happens only after the commit. The same approach was applied to targeted quotes and quote status changes.
problems.result: Rolled-back quotes no longer send notifications. "Send only on success, never on a unique-constraint violation" is pinned down with unit tests.

problems.title: About 120 refetches for every single message received
problems.problem: Every incoming chat message triggered about 120 refetches.
problems.cause: Each Realtime event reloaded the whole chat room list (rooms) and the message pages.
problems.fix: I updated the cache directly from the event payload and put a 300ms debounce on the remaining refetches.
problems.result: Refetches per received message dropped from about 120 to at most 1.

problems.title: Why we moved real-time chat from Supabase Realtime to Socket.IO
problems.problem: We first built chat quickly on Supabase Realtime without a separate socket server, but limits showed up in operation.
problems.cause: We had to manage the main DB and Supabase together, the free plan had event limits, and interactions that aren't stored in the DB, like a typing indicator, were hard to handle.
problems.fix: In the second iteration I switched to Socket.IO, consolidated messages into the single main DB, and stored chat images in S3.
problems.result: DB management became a single concern, and we could add chat UX such as a typing indicator.

problems.title: An LCP stretched by late-starting image requests
problems.problem: Lighthouse showed long LCP on several pages, and even after cutting image and font sizes, some pages barely improved.
problems.cause: The shared ProfileImage could not receive a priority-loading option, so even the first image at the top of the screen was lazy-loaded and its request started late.
problems.fix: I converted 8 static images to WebP (3.62MB → 169KB) and kept only the glyphs Pretendard actually uses (2.06MB → 171KB). I also added a priority prop to ProfileImage and applied it only to the first card in the list.
problems.result: Mobile performance went from 43.5 to 78.8 and desktop from 65.0 to 95.4. LCP dropped from 15.62s to 6.30s on mobile and from 2.85s to 1.37s on desktop.

problems.title: Auto-scroll and read receipts stopping in long conversations
problems.problem: In chat rooms with many messages, read receipts and auto-scroll occasionally didn't run even when a new message arrived.
problems.cause: New messages were detected by messages.length. Because pages of 10 are cached, the array length could stay the same even when a new message arrived.
problems.fix: I changed read receipts and scrolling to trigger on the last message ID instead of the array length.
problems.result: The same symptom hasn't been reported since, and the latest message is detected regardless of how many messages there are.

performance.lead: I measured 37 page and device pairs before and after the improvements. Figures are shown per device.
head: Device
Pairs
Performance (before → after)
LCP (before → after)
Accessibility (before → after)
performance.note: The screens that changed most are the mover's sent-quote detail (desktop 39 → 100, mobile 27 → 85) and the sent-quote list (desktop 41 → 100, mobile 31 → 84).

retro.title: What I learned
paragraphs: Real-time delivery is a side effect outside the transaction, so it isn't rolled back. Events that leave the system have to wait until after the commit.
Even small images lengthen LCP if their request starts late. Give priority only to the actual LCP element.

retro.title: Next steps
paragraphs: Mobile LCP still has room to improve at an average of 6.30s. I plan to render the first data earlier with server prefetch and HydrationBoundary.
SSE connections live in memory, so this assumes a single server. Scaling out would require Redis pub/sub.

k-test.title: K-TEST
oneLiner: A service where foreign workers take a job and safety Korean speaking test online,
from identity verification to the result report
k-test.hero: Key screen capture — speaking question screen · 16:9 video

intro.body: Test takers complete identity verification with their ID, face and earphone checks, then go through dual-monitor guidance and calibration before answering speaking questions. During the test, cheating is detected through browser events and webcam analysis, and afterwards they can review the scoring report and their test history.
screens: Identity verification · ID and face check

scope.title: Test flow
items: Built the entire test flow: identity verification → face → earphone check → calibration → questions → completion
Redesigned around pre-created sessions to match a change in the exam plan (new, resume and re-verify branches)
Blocked question exposure before the status lookup with an access guard (canAccess)

scope.title: Test screens
items: Speaking question renderer (image, text and audio sections)
Recorded answer upload
ProctorGuard (browser event detection) · WebcamMonitor (webcam analysis)
Adaptive webcam frame sampling: low frequency normally, shorter intervals when a violation is detected, balancing server load and detection delay

scope.title: Results · foundation
items: Test history, scoring report and violation details of disqualified sessions
Zustand (session and test state) + TanStack Query (server state)
Tailwind v4 design tokens and shared UI components

problems.title: Refining cheating detection so honest test takers aren't disqualified
problems.problem: A single tab switch could be logged as several violations, and losing focus while the camera permission prompt was open was mistaken for leaving the tab, so honest test takers could be disqualified.
problems.cause: On one tab switch the browser sends both blur and visibilitychange events. The camera permission prompt also causes a focus loss.
problems.fix: I merged the two simultaneous events into one record and filtered out focus loss while the camera permission prompt is showing so it isn't logged as leaving the tab.
problems.result: Duplicate records and false positives no longer disqualify honest test takers.
problems.capture: Webcam proctoring · violation detection screen capture

problems.title: Waiting on the scoring screen without knowing you were disqualified
problems.problem: The result screen for a disqualified session didn't tell the user they were disqualified and only showed "Scoring…".
problems.cause: A disqualified session is never scored, so no result ID is created, and the polling stop condition had no disqualified state. Users waited up to 60 seconds of needless polling on the "Scoring…" screen without knowing.
problems.fix: I added the disqualified state to the polling stop condition and branched to a dedicated disqualification card and a violation detail page.
problems.result: Disqualified sessions move straight to the disqualification notice without waiting, and the test taker can review the violation details.

problems.title: Identity verification failing after uploading ID and face images
problems.problem: In a flow where ID and face images are uploaded directly to storage through a signed URL, the identity verification request failed.
problems.cause: Checking with the backend, the AI vendor (Azure Document Intelligence) is officially specified at 4MB but only handled about 1MB reliably, and failed from 2.3MB. The existing code only downscaled above 5MB, so smaller files like a phone original (e.g. 4.5MB) were uploaded as is.
problems.fix: I lowered the auto-downscale threshold and target size from 5MB to 1MB. Sensitive images are still uploaded directly via signed URL without passing through the server. PDFs can't be downscaled, so they are uploaded as is even above 1MB.
problems.result: The identity verification request failures were resolved.

problems.title: Recorded voice answers failing to upload with a 415
problems.problem: When uploading a recorded voice answer, the server rejected it with a 415 (unsupported media type).
problems.cause: The MIME type declared when issuing the signed URL differed from the Content-Type of the actual PUT request.
problems.fix: I changed the shared upload function's signature so the contentType declared at issuance is used as is in the PUT, applied it to the four uploads (answer, clip, ID, face), and retried transient failures up to twice with exponential backoff.
problems.result: The voice upload 415 failures are fixed, and transient network errors are retried automatically.

retro.title: What I learned
paragraphs: Owning the whole test flow alone taught me that variables from outside the code, like plan changes and external API limits, also have to be absorbed by the design.
Building only the happy path wasn't enough. States users actually face, like a disqualified session, were always more varied than expected.

retro.title: How I work
paragraphs: I use AI coding tools like Claude Code to speed up implementation, but I form the cause hypotheses and make the design decisions myself.
